data.hypothesis: The catalog reports 11 distinct valid programs. Its measured best is a 128-thread CTA/source tile at 0.00089008 s; compact 224- and 256-thread variants measured about 0.000920 s, and the recent 128-thread variant measured 0.00089338 s. Test a 96-thread CTA with a matching 96-source tile while retaining full-Particle staging and the interaction order, isolating narrower CTA geometry. This uses 2,688 bytes of shared memory, but requires more tiles and barriers per target; no speedup is assumed.
data.notes: The 96-thread tile stages only valid sources in the partial tile; inactive output lanes still reach both CTA barriers, and output bounds are checked before writing. The proposed candidate has not been measured. Await official correctness checks before timing and compare through the official protocol.
transformations: Set block and items_per_block to 96 so each thread owns one target and stages one source per tile lane; use 2,688 bytes for 96 full Particle records.
Stage ascending source tiles in dynamic shared memory, bound source reads for partial tiles, and retain both block-wide barriers so every lane participates before shared data is reused.
Preserve the original force and integration arithmetic, self-interaction skip, target bounds check, and output particle fields.
